text.p: Following are reports carried by Lithuania's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The leader of the Homeland Union party, Vytautas Landsbergis, says that the the most likely candidate for the post of foreign minister in the new government will be the chairman of the Christian Democrats, Algirdas Saudargas.
- Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) will start regular flights between Vilnius and Stockholm on November 4.
- Gitanas Nauseda, head of the Bank of Lithuania's policy department, says that the possible abolition of the currency board does not mean that the litas will be devalued.
- The prosecutor's office questioned alleged war criminal Aleksandras Lileikis for a fourth time.
- The Vilnius district court has started to investigate the case of four former NKVD agents accused of murdering a rural family in the spring of 1945.
- Lithuania was rated at 59, a 26 point jump, in a Euromoney survey which ranking European states' investment climate. Lithuania's ranking was higher than Latvia and Estonia's.
- The Bank of Lithuania has registered 17 million litas worth of share capital for the new Bank of Industry.
